proposals.expected_failure_mode: SEIRS can still be weakly identifiable on 31 training weeks; the added waning parameter may induce split-to-split variability or over-flexibility, potentially shifting peak timing/width without improving generalization.
proposals.rationale: Anchor template per feedback: SEIRS captures potential waning immunity/reinfection effects that may help on a short, high-peaked influenza hospitalization-rate series, while keeping observation mapping simple and stable (direct I proxy, no delay). This is an incremental change from prior SIR/SEIR discoveries and avoids adding extra compartments.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Prior feedback indicates 1-week delay degraded performance for this series; this variant may misalign peak timing (forecast peak too late) and amplify instability/identifiability issues by coupling delay with waning dynamics.
proposals.rationale: Single carefully controlled alternative: retain SEIRS structure but allow a minimal 1-week reporting/admission lag via delayed_I, consistent with surveillance semantics, while respecting the constraint to explore only {0,1} week delays. This isolates whether a small lag improves alignment without changing compartments.
